item.title: Optimize AI economics on Amazon Bedrock with Accenture’s sequenced approach
item.description: As enterprises scale AI on Amazon Bedrock, token spend can grow even as per-token prices fall. This post walks through six composable optimization levers, shows how Accenture applied them across four client engagements, and recommends a sequence for cutting AI token spend on your own workloads. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/optimize-ai-economics-on-amazon-bedrock-with-accentures-sequenced-approach

item.title: From learning to leaderboard: How Cisco upskilled 1,200 engineers in agentic AI with AWS AI League
item.description: Cisco and AWS used Cisco Transformation Fest and AWS AI League to turn hands-on AI learning into a culture of building. A Cisco engineer won the 2025 AWS AI League global title and 1,200 engineers competed in 2026. This post shares Cisco's journey, lessons from the 2026 winning agent built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and how to host your own league. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.

item.title: Keep inference running through regional capacity shortfalls with cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI
item.description: Cross-Region inference routing in Amazon SageMaker AI gives your application one invocation path across the endpoints and inference components you already run, in one or more AWS Regions and AWS accounts. The router prefers its own Region and shifts new requests to another destination only when the local one can't serve reliably. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/keep-inference-running-through-regional-capacity-shortfalls-with-cross-region-inference-routing-in-amazon-sagemaker-ai

item.title: Protect agent tool calls with Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
item.description: Learn how Skyflow and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway keep sensitive data out of the tools your AI agents call. Added as a gateway interceptor, Skyflow de-identifies data before any tool, model, or log sees it, and restores it for authorized callers, with no change to your agent code. Worth a read for developers following AWS and AI. Link to article: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/protect-agent-tool-calls-with-skyflow-and-amazon-bedrock-agentcore-gateway

item.title: Diagnosing thread pool starvation from a .NET dump with an AI agent
item.description: Thread pool starvation does not hang the application, it makes it slow, and it makes it slow in a way that no profiler flags: the CPU is idle, no query is slow, and every individual operation looks fine. What is wrong is that the pool has no thread left to run the next work item, because the previous ones are all blocked waiting for something. This is also the case where an agent saves the most time,…

item.title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
item.description: Microsoft has released ASP.NET Core in .NET 11. The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default. By Almir Vuk Worth a read for developers following .NET and AI. Link to article: https://www.

item.title: Finding a deadlock in a .NET dump with an AI agent
item.description: A hang is the easiest problem to diagnose from a dump and the hardest to diagnose any other way. There is no exception, no log line, and attaching a debugger to a production process is rarely an option. But the state that explains it, which thread holds what and which thread waits for what, is entirely present in a dump. This post takes a deadlocked process and lets an agent find both locks.
